items.markdown:
You can use the [ClinCalc Sample Size Calculator](https://clincalc.com/stats/samplesize.aspx) to determine the minimum number of subjects required for your study to detect a treatment effect.[[1]](https://clincalc.com/stats/samplesize.aspx)

### Key Online Calculators

- **Clinical & General Research:** ClinCalc Sample Size Calculator for dichotomous or continuous endpoints.
- **Proportions & Means:** [UBC Power/Sample Size Calculator](https://www.stat.ubc.ca/~rollin/stats/ssize/b1.html) for single or two-sample comparisons.
- **Hypothesis Tests:** [Numiqo Power Analysis Calculator](https://numiqo.com/statistics-calculator/sample-size/power-analysis-calculator) to switch between *a priori* sample size and post-hoc power calculations.
- **Comprehensive Tests:** [University of Vienna Sample Size Calculator](https://homepage.univie.ac.at/robin.ristl/samplesize.php) for t-tests, ANOVA, Chi-squared, and more.
- **NIH Resources:** [NIH Research Methods Resources](https://researchmethodsresources.nih.gov/Calculators) for complex designs like cluster and group-randomized trials.[[1]](https://homepage.univie.ac.at/robin.ristl/samplesize.php)[[2]](https://clincalc.com/stats/samplesize.aspx)[[3]](https://www.stat.ubc.ca/~rollin/stats/ssize/b1.html)[[4]](https://www.stat.ubc.ca/~rollin/stats/ssize/n2.html)[[5]](https://numiqo.com/statistics-calculator/sample-size)[[6]](https://numiqo.com/statistics-calculator/sample-size/power-analysis-calculator)[[7]](https://researchmethodsresources.nih.gov/Calculators)

### Core Variables Needed for Calculation

- **Effect Size:** The magnitude of the difference you expect to find (such as Cohen's *d* or *w*).
- **Significance Level (α):** The probability of a false positive, usually set at 0.05 (5%).
- **Statistical Power (1 - β):** The probability of detecting a true effect when one exists, usually set at 0.80 (80%).
- **Baseline / Variance:** The expected incidence, mean, or standard deviation in the control or population group.[[1]](https://www.statscalculators.com/calculators/hypothesis-testing/sample-size-and-power-analysis-calculator)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PPHATJhWQcU&t=173)[[3]](https://www.statskingdom.com/sample_size_regression.html)[[4]](https://clincalc.com/stats/samplesize.aspx)[[5]](https://www.gigacalculator.com/calculators/power-sample-size-calculator.php)[[6]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ey4PqVy372U)[[7]](https://clincalc.com/stats/power.aspx)

If you share your **study design** (e.g., two independent means, proportions, or a regression) and your **expected effect size** , I can help you figure out which calculator settings to use.
